newsitem.title: USA: Brady bonds end higher in pre-holiday thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Brady bonds end higher in pre-holiday thin trade.

text.p: Emerging debt prices wound down trading activity earlier than usual on Monday as volume remained very thin amid pre-holiday doldrums, traders said.
Brady bonds in general were seen up by 1/4 to 1/2 points earlier in the trading day boosted by U.S. Treasuries but ended the trading day on a lighter note.
Argentine pars were off 1/8 at 64-1/8 bid, while Argentine discounts bonds were up 1/4 at 77-1/4 bid, traders said.
Brazil "C" bonds were up 1/2 at 74-3/4, Venezuelan Pars were unchanged at 76-3/4 bid and Mexico Pars were up 1/8 at 73-7/8 bid.
Russia's dollar Vnesh was quoted up 1/8 at 79-3/4 bid.
Peru Citi bonds remained unchanged at 116 bid amid the continuing hostage crisis, traders said.

As the crisis moved into its 13th day, rebels belonging to the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement continued to hold 83 hostages in the Japanese ambassador's residence, including top Peruvian officials, foreign diplomats and Japanese businessmen.
Earlier on Monday, Bear Stearns & Co said the Peruvian economy would experience lower-than-expected growth next year due to the current hostage crisis in Lima.

The firm said the attack by leftist rebels on the Japanese Ambassador's residence would likely reduce investment from Japan, have a "less notable" negative impact on other investments and tourism, and "tarnish" the image of Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori.
The firm did not say by how much it would lower its estimate of 1997 Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth. Its original forecast was growth of 4.0 percent to 5.5 percent.
The government's official projection for 1997 economic growth is 5.0 percent.
Trading in Bradies "has been extremely light," said one trader. "Activity wound down by about noon when Europe left the market," one trader said.
Players will see a shortened trading session on Tuesday as the U.S. credit market will shut down at 1400 EST/1900 GMT ahead of Wednesday's New Year's Day holiday when U.S. markets will remain closed.
In U.S. Treasuries, the 30-year bond was off 2/32 at 99-14/32 to yield 6.54 percent.
